claims.claim:
## Incident
Before the Productization branch was created, six GitHub connector commits had already reached `main` while creating and immediately deleting accidental placeholder files. Current tree is restored, but the published commits have no repository-required Driven-By / Driven-On trailers and the connector could not produce the required `.invalid` machine author identity.

Exact published commits:
```text
89c39f83314bee79226af5e081fc2013c41ccc13  add accidental root `x`
55f926e22c13ce6212280819b1eea916d35cd384  remove `x`
8e2c89d120ecb74fcffa4d708d0714ca8583036f  add accidental root `__never__`
5417467f1416ced5a6ad0d1fabaa38f6d850d3e8  remove `__never__`
957d7373a36ae78b6379c28625967090e5b296fc  add accidental root `stop`
ccef97dedd7ea8b1873e3afa130ca82b8eabb413  remove `stop`
```

## Required repair
Use a local/Forgejo/Codex/Claude lane that can author a compliant machine commit. Add exactly these six already-published SHAs to `evals/commit-roles.json::known_unclassified`, with one commit-specific reason each. Do not move `enforced_from`, widen a pattern, rewrite main, or falsely relabel the commits Human.

Run:
```text
python3 scripts/check_commit_roles.py --repo-root .
python3 -m unittest tests/test_commit_roles.py -v
```
and the current owning repository workflows on the exact candidate.

claims.applicability_rationale: Scope/policy constraint on how the required-repair claim (435-required-repair-classify-commits) must be executed once attempted; it names no independent action of its own and has no separate implementation/verification lifecycle to close.
claims.claim:
## Evidence boundary
This only repairs provenance classification for already-published history. It does not admit the Productization PR, product truth, merge, release or runtime behavior.
